conditions: Each chosen day carries a session of a supported family for that sport and profile; the weekly load is set first from goal, recent practice (ONB-08), phase and approved policy, then distributed across the chosen days. The app never drops a chosen day and never invents a frequency ceiling.

Long-run adjacency is handled by content, never by moving days: heaviest lower-body, eccentric-dominant or novel strength work stays away from the day before the long run when the chosen days allow; otherwise lower-body demand is reduced by content and the trade-off explained; in Strength-first the long run's content may flex. On a day with both sports in different shifts, the person's shift choice fixes the order; the coach protects the priority through the content of the earlier session; only the person moves sessions (EDT-02).

HOLD, a reported limitation or an out-of-coverage case may reduce a session, replace it with recovery or retain it, always explained and never by silently removing the day. Persistent pain, injury or illness route to CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED with no substitute dose.

items.approved_scope: Reusable rule for confirmed back-to-back strength and running sessions in the same shift only under every listed condition.
conditions: Back-to-back is allowed only when the person chose the same day and shift for both sports and confirmed 'fazer em sequência'; the confirmation is a changeable preference, not an inference.

The person can always swap the order.
No hour or minute rule and no claim about recovery between the two parts (POL-07).

Where the chosen days allow, avoid a demanding key session of one sport straight before a demanding key session of the other through content allocation, not by moving days; if unavoidable, lower the non-priority session's demand under approved policy and explain it.
A double counts as two sessions, not a third load event or a fatigue score; the combined length is shown only as a logistics fact.

Single-run ceiling (operational.run.singleRunCeiling): no planned run other than the race exceeds the longest completed run of the preceding 30 days (completed-work ledger, the intake-reported longest current run while within 30 days of intake, a valid return demonstration) by more than one stepMinutes; walk/jog ladder sessions and walks follow the ladder, whose start never holds more jogging per session than the longest current run (D42); with nothing completed in the window the reviewed entry (return.entryRunMinutes) is the ceiling in every week, not only the first.

When the 30-day reference run is under 50 minutes, the 5-minute step exceeds 10% of it; the step stays response-gated, is disclosed, and is never combined with another single-session increase in the same week. A long-run step that the long-run share cap holds is not a single-session increase: that week the easy step and the quality step proceed under their own gates and cadence, and if either steps the long-run target waits where it was prescribed. In such a week the stepped easy run may equal the long run prescribed that week, never exceed it. Item 5: a return-entry week is one in which an exercise in use that week is at the entry step; an exercise not in use (rotated out and still parked at the entry step) has no weight. A never-performed exercise, a substitute included, first prescribed after every exercise in use has passed the entry step is established by effort, at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3, with no load converted, and then progresses as a new exercise (NR-21, SUB-6).

D55 (met at R7A-FREEZE-2 and at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): an exercise first set up while the exercises in use are in the return steps of a moderate or long return earns no block-boundary set for the block of the return, as return-entry and return-step exposures do not; after the return steps its count rises at most one set per executed week, up to its normal count (its ceiling under strengthReturnSets), with phase reductions on top. Regression tests: the RS2 scenario (return step 2 in a block-end week, a substitution window) for HYPERTROPHY, STRENGTH and RUNNING_SUPPORT, with EVERY_2_WEEKS (parked exercises) and FIXED rotation.

Item 6: sets logged without repetitions leave the repetition target neither met nor missed; the dose holds without a regression step and repetitions are never adopted from a missing value; a logged reserve below the prescription minus one, or fewer sets than prescribed, remains a missed target.

Item 7: a week whose last executed row of an exercise is below its count before the phase reduction, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, earns no regain, return-cap or return-ceiling set.
Item 8: a missed session moves only to a later chosen day of the same sport whose day phase, by days to the race, equals its own; no move in taper or race week; race touches and shakeouts never move.

S2: on HOLD and REGRESS a log that confirms the known load leaves the repetition target as planned (REGRESS lowers the load one smallest increment, or the repetitions by repStep down to the range floor when no load is known); on ADVANCE or EARNED the logged repetitions may replace it; a newly established load (first establishment or re-establishment by effort) is adopted with the repetitions logged for it. A set without repetitions is unknown, never a missed target.

S3: a return re-plans every session still ahead of the review (later dates, or the same day without an execution report); sessions reported before the review keep their prescription; when re-entry starts the next week, a session still ahead this week waits (rest by design) and never keeps its pre-break dose; a race is never turned into rest.

R27 / QE-R7A-02 (same-day reading, met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): a session is still ahead of a review when it is dated after the review’s local date, or dated that day with no execution report while its chosen shift is not over; a morning (AM) session is over at noon local time, an afternoon or unspecified shift at the end of the day. A short return reported on the morning of a quality day, or the evening before, makes that run easy; an evening report never rewrites that morning’s session. The noon boundary is an operational convention of the shift model, not a physiological threshold. D58 (not met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): in a short return the first quality slot after the break is the first quality slot still ahead of the return report, in the week re-entry starts or a later week; it runs easy, recorded as an adaptation of the week that holds it so a later re-plan and the weekly review keep it; exactly one slot is changed. At R7A1-FREEZE-A1 the rule reaches only the week re-entry starts: when that week’s quality slot is already past and two or more sessions remain, next week’s first quality slot keeps its quality dose (ssctr-r7a1-short.mjs: 96 of 315 cases, also after the weekly review; in a 10-day break THRESHOLD 41 where the last executed was 34), so this clause is outside the approval until a later freeze meets it. Regression: the short grid’s defects at 0 after the return and after the review.

S4/S9: when an event change moves any remaining day of the current week into or out of the taper, race-window or post-event days, or the race itself is still ahead this week, those days are re-planned under the new phases by days to the race (proximitySemantics), with completed sessions unchanged; a goal change that only renames a training phase applies from the next week.

S5: a missed session is moved only to a later chosen day of the same sport, in the same day phase, where every strength row keeps its kind on the new date (a known or from-log row never becomes a re-establishment by moving, nor the reverse); otherwise it is skipped without debt.

S6: a fatigue reduction lowers the recorded count and makes the week reduced; the return ceiling is the largest whole count executed that week outside a phase reduction, each exposure counted after its time fit (R20).

D56 (final formulation, R7A1-SSCTR-r1 S1): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when the last executed exposure of the exercise that week, the one that gives the week’s counts (R19, INV-04), executed its count before the phase reduction after its time fit. Any other week neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps); the return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is the largest whole count executed after the fit (R20). Met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 for the rise of both caps and for the regain cap; not met for the end of the return cap (D57). D57 (not met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1): see R7A1-SSCTR-D56-FORMULATION.
S7: a week planned as a return-entry week stays one when its remaining days are rebuilt; every new exercise in it gets the entry dose in every time budget and follows the return steps.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

Reading (a): a quality run already eased by another adaptation is not the return’s easy slot; the slot is the first session still ahead that would run at quality dose. Not named in the dossier, accepted: a slot made easy and not done (missed or unreported) does not pass on; the next quality session is at the held dose (the missed-session rule). A short break whose week holds no quality slot carries the slot to the next week placed that holds one, across a race touch, a race and a post-event week (R32, R33 for the next policy revision).

D59 (open, blocking; outside this approval): the return starts from the strength state at the start of the pause week, so an exercise whose first executed exposures fall in that week before the break loses them. R27 / QE-R7A-02 (same-day reading, met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 and at R7A1-FREEZE-A2): a session is still ahead of a review when it is dated after the review’s local date, or dated that day with no execution report while its chosen shift is not over; a morning (AM) session is over at noon local time, an afternoon or unspecified shift at the end of the day. A short return reported on the morning of a quality day, or the evening before, makes that run easy; an evening report never rewrites that morning’s session. The noon boundary is an operational convention of the shift model, not a physiological threshold.

D58 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2): in a short return the first quality slot still ahead of the return report (C1), in the week re-entry starts or a later week, runs easy, recorded on the week that holds it so later re-plans and the weekly review keep it; exactly one slot is changed; the readings of "still ahead" when other adaptations meet it are ruled in R7A1-SSCTR-QUALITY-SLOT-READINGS. Regression: the short grid at 0 after the return and after the review, and tests "R7-A.1 C4/C5 (D58)" and "R7-A.1 C4 (D58)".

A same-day equipment change re-plans the strength sessions still ahead that day; a never-performed substitute gets the effort-guided establishment (at most 2 sets at RIR 3 or more, no load converted); sessions reported before the change keep their rows (met).

D59 (open, blocking; outside this approval): the return starts from the strength state at the start of the pause week, so an exercise whose first executed exposures fall in that week before the break loses them. When the pause week is the athlete’s first loaded week, no exercise is in use at the return, no week is an entry week, and every exercise executed before the break restarts as a first establishment (up to 2 sets at RIR 3, not strengthEntrySets at strengthEntryMinimumRir or more), earns the block set of the block in progress and comes back above its declared ceiling, up to two sets above the largest count since the return (R7A1-SSCTR-D59-PAUSE-WEEK-START). This approval does not cover the start state of a return.
The readings of "the first quality slot still ahead" when other adaptations meet it, when the slot is not done and near a race are those of R7A1-SSCTR-QUALITY-SLOT-READINGS.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

After a performed re-establishment by effort (more than return.moderateMaxDays since the last executed exposure), the earlier count, block-boundary set included, comes back at most one set per executed week, never at once, whatever the state mode at the re-establishment (known load, pending establishment log, unlogged or re-established) (D53, resolved).

The regain base is the re-establishment count before its phase reduction: min(goal sets for the role, 2, the count the exercise would otherwise have that day). A re-establishment reduced by its phase is followed by that count itself, as a phase-reduced return step 2 is followed by the step-2 count (Q1, reading A).

The cap rises by one set only after a week whose last executed exposure of the exercise executed its whole count (executed sets equal to its count before the phase reduction, gate ADVANCE or EARNED, a logged set); a week whose executed row was below that count, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, never raises it. A phase week whose reduction did not bring the row below that count counts as a whole executed week.
Every later count stays at or below the cap, with phase reductions on top, and is never more than one set above the largest count executed since the re-establishment.
Load: a logged load at or after the re-establishment becomes the reference only by the existing adoption rules, never above the re-establishment ceiling (D44, D45).
To be declared in the next policy revision: setsAfterReestablishment states the base before the phase reduction and the whole-count rule, in the words of strengthReturnSets.

Any other week neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps); the return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is the largest whole count executed after the fit (R20). Met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 for the rise of both caps and for the regain cap; met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 for the end of the return cap too (D57 closed). S3: a return re-plans every session still ahead of the review (later dates, or the same day without an execution report); sessions reported before the review keep their prescription; when re-entry starts the next week, a session still ahead this week waits (rest by design) and never keeps its pre-break dose; a race is never turned into rest.

S5 (C5): a session dated before a return reported the same week is never moved into the re-entry and never counts as done in next week’s conditional plan; a lift not done since the break starts at the return entry (strengthEntrySets at RIR at least strengthEntryMinimumRir), never at a later step without an entry; a newer report of a break that began this week starts from the start the week had before an earlier report of it, so a corrected report plans the week as the corrected report alone (met).

S6 (C3): once the week is complete, its evidence decides next week’s start whatever handler re-plans (an unreported complete week holds); while the week is under way, the conditional plan of the week as now planned decides, its rows assumed executed as prescribed except sessions dated before a return; a return’s re-base of next week is kept; the weekly review re-derives the start from evidence (met).

S6 (run ceiling): in a conditional projection the earlier projected weeks count as executed for the single-run ceiling, as the policy states; the first week a review projects uses completed runs only (met).

Item 5: a return-entry week is one in which an exercise in use that week is at the entry step; an exercise not in use (rotated out and still parked at the entry step) has no weight. A never-performed exercise, a substitute included, first prescribed after every exercise in use has passed the entry step is established by effort, at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3, with no load converted, and then progresses as a new exercise (NR-21, SUB-6).

D55 (met at R7A-FREEZE-2, at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 and at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE): an exercise first set up while the exercises in use are in the return steps of a moderate or long return earns no block-boundary set for the block of the return, as return-entry and return-step exposures do not; after the return steps its count rises at most one set per executed week, up to its normal count (its ceiling under strengthReturnSets), with phase reductions on top. Regression tests: the RS2 scenario (return step 2 in a block-end week, a substitution window) for HYPERTROPHY, STRENGTH and RUNNING_SUPPORT, with EVERY_2_WEEKS (parked exercises) and FIXED rotation.

Item 6: sets logged without repetitions leave the repetition target neither met nor missed; the dose holds without a regression step and repetitions are never adopted from a missing value; a logged reserve below the prescription minus one, or fewer sets than prescribed, remains a missed target.

Item 7: a week whose last executed row of an exercise is below its count before the phase reduction, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, earns no regain, return-cap or return-ceiling set.
Item 8: a missed session moves only to a later chosen day of the same sport whose day phase, by days to the race, equals its own; no move in taper or race week; race touches and shakeouts never move.

D59 (met at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE, closed): a return starts from the state at the break (stateAtBreak, strengthAtBreak): every exercise executed before the break’s first day is in use with its last performed date and, outside a return step and a phase reduction, its last executed whole count after the time fit (target met) as the ceiling (the largest of the break week, R20); a moderate or long return enters it at strengthEntrySets with strengthEntryMinimumRir or more, step 2 follows, the block in progress earns no set and the count comes back at most one set per executed whole week up to the ceiling; the progression the pre-break exposures earned stays unapplied. Regression: ssctr-r7a1-recheck-firstweek.mjs with E, O and B at 0 for NONE and FAMILIAR and O at 0 for KNOWN, my restoration, cap and short grids, and test "R7-A.2 I4/I5/I8 (SSCTR D59)".

The start state of a return is the state at its interruption under R7A2-SSCTR-INTERRUPTION-STATE (revision R7AF-SSCTR-r1) and INTERRUPTION_EPISODE_CONTRACT R7AF-INTERRUPTION-1: a correction names its interruption (episodeId) or repeats its days and starts from what the athlete had executed at its own start; a break after a re-entry or after training is new and starts from that re-entry plus the facts executed since; anything else is asked; each short break owns its easy slot.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

S2: on HOLD and REGRESS a log that confirms the known load leaves the repetition target as planned (REGRESS lowers the load one smallest increment, or the repetitions by repStep down to the range floor when no load is known); on ADVANCE or EARNED the logged repetitions may replace it; a newly established load (first establishment or re-establishment by effort) is adopted with the repetitions logged for it. A set without repetitions is unknown, never a missed target.

S3: a return re-plans every session still ahead of the review (later dates, or the same day without an execution report); sessions reported before the review keep their prescription; when re-entry starts the next week, a session still ahead this week waits (rest by design) and never keeps its pre-break dose; a race is never turned into rest.

R27 / QE-R7A-02 (same-day reading, met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 and at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE): a session is still ahead of a review when it is dated after the review’s local date, or dated that day with no execution report while its chosen shift is not over; a morning (AM) session is over at noon local time, an afternoon or unspecified shift at the end of the day. A short return reported on the morning of a quality day, or the evening before, makes that run easy; an evening report never rewrites that morning’s session. The noon boundary is an operational convention of the shift model, not a physiological threshold. D58 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE): in a short return the first quality slot still ahead of the return report (C1), in the week re-entry starts or a later week, runs easy, recorded on the week that holds it so later re-plans and the weekly review keep it; exactly one slot is changed; the readings of "still ahead" when other adaptations meet it are ruled in R7A1-SSCTR-QUALITY-SLOT-READINGS. Regression: the short grid at 0 after the return and after the review, and tests "R7-A.1 C4/C5 (D58)" and "R7-A.1 C4 (D58)".

S4/S9: when an event change moves any remaining day of the current week into or out of the taper, race-window or post-event days, or the race itself is still ahead this week, those days are re-planned under the new phases by days to the race (proximitySemantics), with completed sessions unchanged; a goal change that only renames a training phase applies from the next week.

S5: a missed session is moved only to a later chosen day of the same sport, in the same day phase, where every strength row keeps its kind on the new date (a known or from-log row never becomes a re-establishment by moving, nor the reverse); otherwise it is skipped without debt.

S6: a fatigue reduction lowers the recorded count and makes the week reduced; the return ceiling is the largest whole count executed that week outside a phase reduction, each exposure counted after its time fit (R20).

D56 (final formulation, R7A1-SSCTR-r1 S1): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when the last executed exposure of the exercise that week, the one that gives the week’s counts (R19, INV-04), executed its count before the phase reduction after its time fit. Any other week neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps); the return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is the largest whole count executed after the fit (R20). Met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 for the rise of both caps and for the regain cap; met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 for the end of the return cap too (D57 closed). D57 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE): the return cap rises and ends only after a week whose last executed exposure did its whole count after its time fit, and ends only when it is at or above next week’s normal count with the block-boundary set that transition earns (phase reductions on top); the regain cap ends only at the largest count the exercise can have. No count after a re-establishment or a return exceeds the largest count executed since then by more than one set, for every exercise a cap or the return steps cover (B = 0 over the 864 and 360 timelines of my grids). The end test reads next week’s count as this week’s normal count plus the block set; another rise of the normal count at a transition (the NONE-class first-block clamp, a priorSets regain) was not reached with a cap in force (observation N4). Regression: the grid’s A, B and C at 0 and test "R7-A.1 D57" (both parts).
S7: a week planned as a return-entry week stays one when its remaining days are rebuilt; every new exercise in it gets the entry dose in every time budget and follows the return steps.

S-A (approved): an exercise first executed in the break’s week enters a moderate or long return at the entry, with its last executed whole count as the ceiling; E, O, B and ceiling disagreements at 0 in every class and length measured.

S-B (approved): after a short break a loaded exercise whose first log the break left unadopted is established by effort again (UNLOGGED, at most effortGuidedLoad.sets = 2, RIR 3 or more, at its executed repetitions); a bodyweight exercise set up before a short break continues at its normal count. Never above the last executed count or 2, never above the no-break timeline’s week.

S-C (approved as the declared reading): an exposure that missed its logged target is performed (in use) but gives no ceiling count; the ceiling falls back as declared (the earlier executed count, else the known count, else the normal count). Rises stay one set per executed whole week, gated on post-return targets (R36 records the met/missed asymmetry for the next policy revision).

S-D (approved): a re-establishment executed before a break is a fact: a moderate or long return takes the re-establishment count as the ceiling; after a short break the load is established by effort again (at most 2 sets, under the earlier load) and the count comes back one set per executed whole week (D53). R35 records the cost for the next policy revision.

S-E (approved): each short break owns its easy slot; a separate later short break takes the first quality slot still ahead that no break has eased (reading a: an eased run is no longer a quality slot), so when the first break’s slot is still ahead both run easy; a newer report of the same break keeps its slot; exactly one slot per break.

S-F (approved): a short break during the return steps resumes the step reached; a weekly review decided after the break began does not count, so the entry may repeat once (conservative); nothing returns to the dose before an earlier break.
S-G (approved): the entry repetition target of an exercise first executed before the break is the one it was executed at.

S-H (superseded by F-D): Training before the latest interruption logged after its return is confirmed first: while that return sets the plan (its re-entry week), every other report asks to confirm the interruption again, and the newer report reads the whole record (entry and ceiling as read in time). This replaces the R7-A.2 S-H/R37 boundary; the cost of what the pending question holds back is NF-R7AF-1 (routed, R38).

F-A (approved): a separate interruption after a re-entry starts from that re-entry plus the facts executed since, whatever reports of the earlier interruption came later; nothing returns to the dose before the earlier interruption; ceilings stay those of the first return.

F-B (approved): after an earlier interruption’s return, a re-entry week neither reviewed nor executed as planned is not a starting point; a later interruption starts from the re-entry plus the executed facts (the entry repeats, as S-F), on either side of a week boundary; a reviewed re-entry week’s decided start is used.

F-C (approved): A strength session on an interruption’s first day is ordered by the interruption’s stated start time: a session completed before that time is in the state (entry, that day’s count as the ceiling), one completed after it is not; with dates only it is asked when its order changes a fact the return starts from (in use, ceiling, unlogged load), and when only a last performed date differs the earlier date is kept (the conservative reading for a re-establishment threshold). This replaces the R7-A.2 NF-1 boundary.

F-D (approved, with NF-R7AF-1 routed as R38): Training before the latest interruption logged after its return is confirmed first: while that return sets the plan (its re-entry week), every other report asks to confirm the interruption again, and the newer report reads the whole record (entry and ceiling as read in time). This replaces the R7-A.2 S-H/R37 boundary; the cost of what the pending question holds back is NF-R7AF-1 (routed, R38).

F-E (approved): an interruption first reported after a later one began is that later interruption’s starting point (the start its report set; sessions between its end and its report belong to the plan before it, C5); a conservative reading.

F-F (approved as Founder-decided ASK, with NF-R7AF-2 routed as R39): a date-shifted correction without the interruption’s name is asked; a named one re-derives exactly as before; the same days are a duplicate; a clinical reason routes to qualified assessment before identity is considered.

D56, D57 and D58 hold on R7A2-FREEZE-1 and on R7A-FINAL-FREEZE: no cap rises or ends after a week whose last exposure was not whole, no covered count comes back more than one set above the largest since the break, and the first quality slot still ahead of a short return runs easy, once per break.
Weekly-review contract as in every record (R18).

Every strength row, the re-establishment row included, takes its day phase once: sets = min(row cap, phase dose of the count the exercise would otherwise have that day), reps in reserve >= max(row floor, phase minimum); the day phase follows days to the race (proximitySemantics).

Race window and post-event: main lifts only, at most raceWeekStrengthSets / postEventStrengthSets set(s) at RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir; one race-window session at most, on the strength day furthest from the race and none in the last raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days. Taper and specific rows keep RIR >= 3 (D54, resolved).

A re-establishment row is never above min(goal sets for its role, 2) and never above the phase dose of the exercise's own count that day; it may be below min(goal sets, 2) when that phase dose or the exercise's own count is lower (consolidation, specific, a known dose of 1 set) (Q2).
At a re-establishment the load stays effort-guided under the earlier ceiling; no load increase, new exercise or rotation in taper or race week.
The final validation rejects any strength row above its day phase dose or below the phase minimum reps in reserve, whatever branch built it.

D59 (met at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE, closed): a return starts from the state at the break (stateAtBreak, strengthAtBreak): every exercise executed before the break’s first day is in use with its last performed date and, outside a return step and a phase reduction, its last executed whole count after the time fit (target met) as the ceiling (the largest of the break week, R20); a moderate or long return enters it at strengthEntrySets with strengthEntryMinimumRir or more, step 2 follows, the block in progress earns no set and the count comes back at most one set per executed whole week up to the ceiling; the progression the pre-break exposures earned stays unapplied. Regression: ssctr-r7a1-recheck-firstweek.mjs with E, O and B at 0 for NONE and FAMILIAR and O at 0 for KNOWN, my restoration, cap and short grids, and test "R7-A.2 I4/I5/I8 (SSCTR D59)".

The start state of a return is the state at its interruption under R7A2-SSCTR-INTERRUPTION-STATE (revision R7AB-SSCTR-r1), INTERRUPTION_EPISODE_CONTRACT R7AF-INTERRUPTION-1 and WEEK_START_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT R7AB-WEEKSTART-1: a correction names its interruption (episodeId) or repeats its days and starts from what the athlete had executed at its own start; a break after a re-entry or after training is new and starts from that re-entry plus the facts executed since; a week start is the state point only when it is evidence-anchored (the intake, a return’s entry, the weekly review’s rule on the complete week before, or a projection the week before executed exactly as it assumed, loads included), otherwise the point moves back to the last such start, before any return too, and the sessions executed after it are facts only; a named correction that contradicts its own executed re-entry is asked; anything else is asked; each short break owns its easy slot.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

Regression tests: the RS2 scenario (return step 2 in a block-end week, a substitution window) for HYPERTROPHY, STRENGTH and RUNNING_SUPPORT, with EVERY_2_WEEKS (parked exercises) and FIXED rotation.

Item 6: sets logged without repetitions leave the repetition target neither met nor missed; the dose holds without a regression step and repetitions are never adopted from a missing value; a logged reserve below the prescription minus one, or fewer sets than prescribed, remains a missed target.

Item 7: a week whose last executed row of an exercise is below its count before the phase reduction, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, earns no regain, return-cap or return-ceiling set.
Item 8: a missed session moves only to a later chosen day of the same sport whose day phase, by days to the race, equals its own; no move in taper or race week; race touches and shakeouts never move.

S2: on HOLD and REGRESS a log that confirms the known load leaves the repetition target as planned (REGRESS lowers the load one smallest increment, or the repetitions by repStep down to the range floor when no load is known); on ADVANCE or EARNED the logged repetitions may replace it; a newly established load (first establishment or re-establishment by effort) is adopted with the repetitions logged for it. A set without repetitions is unknown, never a missed target.

S3: a return re-plans every session still ahead of the review (later dates, or the same day without an execution report); sessions reported before the review keep their prescription; when re-entry starts the next week, a session still ahead this week waits (rest by design) and never keeps its pre-break dose; a race is never turned into rest.

R27 / QE-R7A-02 (same-day reading, met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 and at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE): a session is still ahead of a review when it is dated after the review’s local date, or dated that day with no execution report while its chosen shift is not over; a morning (AM) session is over at noon local time, an afternoon or unspecified shift at the end of the day. A short return reported on the morning of a quality day, or the evening before, makes that run easy; an evening report never rewrites that morning’s session. The noon boundary is an operational convention of the shift model, not a physiological threshold. D58 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE): in a short return the first quality slot still ahead of the return report (C1), in the week re-entry starts or a later week, runs easy, recorded on the week that holds it so later re-plans and the weekly review keep it; exactly one slot is changed; the readings of "still ahead" when other adaptations meet it are ruled in R7A1-SSCTR-QUALITY-SLOT-READINGS. Regression: the short grid at 0 after the return and after the review, and tests "R7-A.1 C4/C5 (D58)" and "R7-A.1 C4 (D58)".

S4/S9: when an event change moves any remaining day of the current week into or out of the taper, race-window or post-event days, or the race itself is still ahead this week, those days are re-planned under the new phases by days to the race (proximitySemantics), with completed sessions unchanged; a goal change that only renames a training phase applies from the next week.

S5: a missed session is moved only to a later chosen day of the same sport, in the same day phase, where every strength row keeps its kind on the new date (a known or from-log row never becomes a re-establishment by moving, nor the reverse); otherwise it is skipped without debt.

S6: a fatigue reduction lowers the recorded count and makes the week reduced; the return ceiling is the largest whole count executed that week outside a phase reduction, each exposure counted after its time fit (R20).

D56 (final formulation, R7A1-SSCTR-r1 S1): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when the last executed exposure of the exercise that week, the one that gives the week’s counts (R19, INV-04), executed its count before the phase reduction after its time fit. Any other week neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps); the return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is the largest whole count executed after the fit (R20). Met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 for the rise of both caps and for the regain cap; met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 for the end of the return cap too (D57 closed). D57 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE): the return cap rises and ends only after a week whose last executed exposure did its whole count after its time fit, and ends only when it is at or above next week’s normal count with the block-boundary set that transition earns (phase reductions on top); the regain cap ends only at the largest count the exercise can have. No count after a re-establishment or a return exceeds the largest count executed since then by more than one set, for every exercise a cap or the return steps cover (B = 0 over the 864 and 360 timelines of my grids). The end test reads next week’s count as this week’s normal count plus the block set; another rise of the normal count at a transition (the NONE-class first-block clamp, a priorSets regain) was not reached with a cap in force (observation N4). Regression: the grid’s A, B and C at 0 and test "R7-A.1 D57" (both parts).
S7: a week planned as a return-entry week stays one when its remaining days are rebuilt; every new exercise in it gets the entry dose in every time budget and follows the return steps.

D59 (met at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE, closed): a return starts from the state at the break (stateAtBreak, strengthAtBreak): every exercise executed before the break’s first day is in use with its last performed date and, outside a return step and a phase reduction, its last executed whole count after the time fit (target met) as the ceiling (the largest of the break week, R20); a moderate or long return enters it at strengthEntrySets with strengthEntryMinimumRir or more, step 2 follows, the block in progress earns no set and the count comes back at most one set per executed whole week up to the ceiling; the progression the pre-break exposures earned stays unapplied. Regression: ssctr-r7a1-recheck-firstweek.mjs with E, O and B at 0 for NONE and FAMILIAR and O at 0 for KNOWN, my restoration, cap and short grids, and test "R7-A.2 I4/I5/I8 (SSCTR D59)".
The readings of "the first quality slot still ahead" when other adaptations meet it, when the slot is not done and near a race are those of R7A1-SSCTR-QUALITY-SLOT-READINGS.

The start state of a return is the state at its interruption under R7A2-SSCTR-INTERRUPTION-STATE (revision R7AB-SSCTR-r1), INTERRUPTION_EPISODE_CONTRACT R7AF-INTERRUPTION-1 and WEEK_START_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT R7AB-WEEKSTART-1: a correction names its interruption (episodeId) or repeats its days and starts from what the athlete had executed at its own start; a break after a re-entry or after training is new and starts from that re-entry plus the facts executed since; a week start is the state point only when it is evidence-anchored (the intake, a return’s entry, the weekly review’s rule on the complete week before, or a projection the week before executed exactly as it assumed, loads included), otherwise the point moves back to the last such start, before any return too, and the sessions executed after it are facts only; a named correction that contradicts its own executed re-entry is asked; anything else is asked; each short break owns its easy slot.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

S-A (approved): an exercise first executed in the break’s week enters a moderate or long return at the entry, with its last executed whole count as the ceiling; E, O, B and ceiling disagreements at 0 in every class and length measured.

S-B (approved): after a short break a loaded exercise whose first log the break left unadopted is established by effort again (UNLOGGED, at most effortGuidedLoad.sets = 2, RIR 3 or more, at its executed repetitions); a bodyweight exercise set up before a short break continues at its normal count. Never above the last executed count or 2, never above the no-break timeline’s week.

S-C (approved as the declared reading): an exposure that missed its logged target is performed (in use) but gives no ceiling count; the ceiling falls back as declared (the earlier executed count, else the known count, else the normal count). Rises stay one set per executed whole week, gated on post-return targets (R36 records the met/missed asymmetry for the next policy revision).

S-D (approved): a re-establishment executed before a break is a fact: a moderate or long return takes the re-establishment count as the ceiling; after a short break the load is established by effort again (at most 2 sets, under the earlier load) and the count comes back one set per executed whole week (D53). R35 records the cost for the next policy revision.

S-E (approved): each short break owns its easy slot; a separate later short break takes the first quality slot still ahead that no break has eased (reading a: an eased run is no longer a quality slot), so when the first break’s slot is still ahead both run easy; a newer report of the same break keeps its slot; exactly one slot per break.

S-F (approved): a short break during the return steps resumes the step reached; a weekly review decided after the break began does not count, so the entry may repeat once (conservative); nothing returns to the dose before an earlier break. R7AB-SSCTR-r1: the step reached is the evidence-anchored one (WEEK_START_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT §3-§4); steps executed after the last evidence-anchored start are facts only, so on an unconsolidated re-entry week the entry may repeat after more than one executed week, and a strength-only shortfall also repeats the run entry (conservative; NF-R7AB-1, routed as R40).
S-G (approved): the entry repetition target of an exercise first executed before the break is the one it was executed at.

S-H (superseded by F-D): Training before the latest interruption logged after its return is confirmed first: while that return sets the plan (its re-entry week), every other report asks to confirm the interruption again, and the newer report reads the whole record (entry and ceiling as read in time). This replaces the R7-A.2 S-H/R37 boundary; the cost of what the pending question holds back is NF-R7AF-1 (routed, R38).

F-A (approved): a separate interruption after a re-entry starts from that re-entry plus the facts executed since, whatever reports of the earlier interruption came later; nothing returns to the dose before the earlier interruption; ceilings stay those of the first return.

F-B (approved): after an earlier interruption’s return, a re-entry week neither reviewed nor executed as planned is not a starting point; a later interruption starts from the re-entry plus the executed facts (the entry repeats, as S-F), on either side of a week boundary; a reviewed re-entry week’s decided start is used.

F-C (approved): A strength session on an interruption’s first day is ordered by the interruption’s stated start time: a session completed before that time is in the state (entry, that day’s count as the ceiling), one completed after it is not; with dates only it is asked when its order changes a fact the return starts from (in use, ceiling, unlogged load), and when only a last performed date differs the earlier date is kept (the conservative reading for a re-establishment threshold). This replaces the R7-A.2 NF-1 boundary.

F-D (approved, with NF-R7AF-1 routed as R38): Training before the latest interruption logged after its return is confirmed first: while that return sets the plan (its re-entry week), every other report asks to confirm the interruption again, and the newer report reads the whole record (entry and ceiling as read in time). This replaces the R7-A.2 S-H/R37 boundary; the cost of what the pending question holds back is NF-R7AF-1 (routed, R38).

F-E (approved): an interruption first reported after a later one began is that later interruption’s starting point (the start its report set; sessions between its end and its report belong to the plan before it, C5); a conservative reading.

F-F (approved as Founder-decided ASK, with NF-R7AF-2 routed as R39): a date-shifted correction without the interruption’s name is asked; a named one re-derives exactly as before; the same days are a duplicate; a clinical reason routes to qualified assessment before identity is considered.

D56, D57 and D58 hold on R7A2-FREEZE-1 and on R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and on R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE: no cap rises or ends after a week whose last exposure was not whole, no covered count comes back more than one set above the largest since the break, and the first quality slot still ahead of a short return runs easy, once per break.

R7AB S-A (approved): after an unfinished, unreviewed re-entry week, a later interruption starts from the re-entry plus the executed facts, whatever was decided meanwhile (equipment, fatigue, schedule, goal or event changes, a no-op statement); only the weekly review’s rule on the complete week, by a review or a handler applying it, may step what was executed in it, and the run holds when a run was missed.

R7AB S-B (approved, with NF-R7AB-1 routed as R40): completed sessions anchor a projected start only when the week executed exactly as the projection assumed, loads included; a lighter effort-guided load leaves the start to a review (which adopts it) or to the re-entry plus facts; a known load the athlete did not lift is never prescribed from a projection.

R7AB S-C (approved): a first interruption after an unconsolidated week moves back to the last evidence-anchored start; on a never-logged program this is the intake: runs from the intake capacity and return target, a known exercise at its reported load, an exercise never performed by the first-exposure establishment (D51, D52; effortGuidedLoad, at most 2 sets at RIR 3 or more), never a return step of a count or load the plan only assumed; with a known exercise in the return steps, exercises first set up in the entry week follow the entry (1 set, RIR 4 or more).
R7AB S-D (approved, with NF-R7AB-1): inside a return, a value a review held from a projected start is not history until a week is executed in full; a later short interruption resumes it at the entry.

R7AB S-E (approved as the Founder-decided ASK, §11): a named correction that puts its interruption on or after training executed after its own return began is asked when it changes a prescription; the plan in force stays the first return’s; no pre-break dose is restored.
R7AB S-F (approved): no unexecuted return step, load or whole count reaches a ceiling or a resumed dose through a stored start (D49, D53, D56).
Weekly-review contract as in every record (R18).

A logged load of an exposure that prescribed a known load is progression evidence: HOLD and REGRESS keep the planned repetition target (REGRESS lowers the load one smallest increment, or the repetitions by repStep down to the range floor when no load is known); ADVANCE or EARNED takes the logged repetitions as at the planned load, the prescription staying inside the goal’s range (met).
A lighter logged load is adopted only under the existing adoption rules, never above a re-establishment ceiling; a heavier one only when that exposure met the ADVANCE criterion (D44, D45) (met).
Only an establishment exposure (first establishment, re-establishment, return entry, from-log) sets its target from its logged repetitions (met).

D59 (met at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE and at STATE-EVIDENCE-FREEZE-1, closed): a return starts from the state at the break (stateAtBreak, strengthAtBreak): every exercise executed before the break’s first day is in use with its last performed date and, outside a return step and a phase reduction, its last executed whole count after the time fit (target met) as the ceiling (the largest of the break week, R20); a moderate or long return enters it at strengthEntrySets with strengthEntryMinimumRir or more, step 2 follows, the block in progress earns no set and the count comes back at most one set per executed whole week up to the ceiling; the progression the pre-break exposures earned stays unapplied. After a performed re-establishment by effort (more than return.moderateMaxDays since the last executed exposure), the earlier count, block-boundary set included, comes back at most one set per executed week, never at once, whatever the state mode at the re-establishment (known load, pending establishment log, unlogged or re-established) (D53, resolved).

The regain base is the re-establishment count before its phase reduction: min(goal sets for the role, 2, the count the exercise would otherwise have that day). A re-establishment reduced by its phase is followed by that count itself, as a phase-reduced return step 2 is followed by the step-2 count (Q1, reading A).

The cap rises by one set only after a week whose last executed exposure of the exercise executed its whole count (executed sets equal to its count before the phase reduction, gate ADVANCE or EARNED, a logged set); a week whose executed row was below that count, by its phase or by an in-week fatigue reduction, never raises it. A phase week whose reduction did not bring the row below that count counts as a whole executed week.
Every later count stays at or below the cap, with phase reductions on top, and is never more than one set above the largest count executed since the re-establishment.
Load: a logged load at or after the re-establishment becomes the reference only by the existing adoption rules, never above the re-establishment ceiling (D44, D45).
To be declared in the next policy revision: setsAfterReestablishment states the base before the phase reduction and the whole-count rule, in the words of strengthReturnSets.

D56 (final formulation, R7A1-SSCTR-r1 S1): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when the last executed exposure of the exercise that week, the one that gives the week’s counts (R19, INV-04), executed its count before the phase reduction after its time fit. Any other week neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps); the return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is the largest whole count executed after the fit (R20). Met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 for the rise of both caps and for the regain cap; met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 for the end of the return cap too (D57 closed). D57 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE and at STATE-EVIDENCE-FREEZE-1): the return cap rises and ends only after a week whose last executed exposure did its whole count after its time fit, and ends only when it is at or above next week’s normal count with the block-boundary set that transition earns (phase reductions on top); the regain cap ends only at the largest count the exercise can have. No count after a re-establishment or a return exceeds the largest count executed since then by more than one set, for every exercise a cap or the return steps cover (B = 0 over the 864 and 360 timelines of my grids). The end test reads next week’s count as this week’s normal count plus the block set; another rise of the normal count at a transition (the NONE-class first-block clamp, a priorSets regain) was not reached with a cap in force (observation N4). Every strength row, the re-establishment row included, takes its day phase once: sets = min(row cap, phase dose of the count the exercise would otherwise have that day), reps in reserve >= max(row floor, phase minimum); the day phase follows days to the race (proximitySemantics).

A re-establishment row is never above min(goal sets for its role, 2) and never above the phase dose of the exercise's own count that day; it may be below min(goal sets, 2) when that phase dose or the exercise's own count is lower (consolidation, specific, a known dose of 1 set) (Q2).
At a re-establishment the load stays effort-guided under the earlier ceiling; no load increase, new exercise or rotation in taper or race week.
The final validation rejects any strength row above its day phase dose or below the phase minimum reps in reserve, whatever branch built it.

S2: on HOLD and REGRESS a log that confirms the known load leaves the repetition target as planned (REGRESS lowers the load one smallest increment, or the repetitions by repStep down to the range floor when no load is known); on ADVANCE or EARNED the logged repetitions may replace it; a newly established load (first establishment or re-establishment by effort) is adopted with the repetitions logged for it. A set without repetitions is unknown, never a missed target.

S3: a return re-plans every session still ahead of the review (later dates, or the same day without an execution report); sessions reported before the review keep their prescription; when re-entry starts the next week, a session still ahead this week waits (rest by design) and never keeps its pre-break dose; a race is never turned into rest.

R27 / QE-R7A-02 (same-day reading, met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 and at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE and at STATE-EVIDENCE-FREEZE-1): a session is still ahead of a review when it is dated after the review’s local date, or dated that day with no execution report while its chosen shift is not over; a morning (AM) session is over at noon local time, an afternoon or unspecified shift at the end of the day. A short return reported on the morning of a quality day, or the evening before, makes that run easy; an evening report never rewrites that morning’s session. The noon boundary is an operational convention of the shift model, not a physiological threshold. D58 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE and at STATE-EVIDENCE-FREEZE-1): in a short return the first quality slot still ahead of the return report (C1), in the week re-entry starts or a later week, runs easy, recorded on the week that holds it so later re-plans and the weekly review keep it; exactly one slot is changed; the readings of "still ahead" when other adaptations meet it are ruled in R7A1-SSCTR-QUALITY-SLOT-READINGS. Regression: the short grid at 0 after the return and after the review, and tests "R7-A.1 C4/C5 (D58)" and "R7-A.1 C4 (D58)".

S4/S9: when an event change moves any remaining day of the current week into or out of the taper, race-window or post-event days, or the race itself is still ahead this week, those days are re-planned under the new phases by days to the race (proximitySemantics), with completed sessions unchanged; a goal change that only renames a training phase applies from the next week.

S5: a missed session is moved only to a later chosen day of the same sport, in the same day phase, where every strength row keeps its kind on the new date (a known or from-log row never becomes a re-establishment by moving, nor the reverse); otherwise it is skipped without debt.

S6: a fatigue reduction lowers the recorded count and makes the week reduced; the return ceiling is the largest whole count executed that week outside a phase reduction, each exposure counted after its time fit (R20).

D56 (final formulation, R7A1-SSCTR-r1 S1): a time-budget fit is not a phase reduction, but a week executed its whole count only when the last executed exposure of the exercise that week, the one that gives the week’s counts (R19, INV-04), executed its count before the phase reduction after its time fit. Any other week neither raises nor ends the regain cap (after a re-establishment) or the return cap (at and after the end of the return steps); the return ceiling (lastExecutedSets) is the largest whole count executed after the fit (R20). Met at R7A1-FREEZE-A1 for the rise of both caps and for the regain cap; met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 for the end of the return cap too (D57 closed). D57 (met at R7A1-FREEZE-A2 and at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE and at STATE-EVIDENCE-FREEZE-1): the return cap rises and ends only after a week whose last executed exposure did its whole count after its time fit, and ends only when it is at or above next week’s normal count with the block-boundary set that transition earns (phase reductions on top); the regain cap ends only at the largest count the exercise can have. No count after a re-establishment or a return exceeds the largest count executed since then by more than one set, for every exercise a cap or the return steps cover (B = 0 over the 864 and 360 timelines of my grids). The end test reads next week’s count as this week’s normal count plus the block set; another rise of the normal count at a transition (the NONE-class first-block clamp, a priorSets regain) was not reached with a cap in force (observation N4). Regression: the grid’s A, B and C at 0 and test "R7-A.1 D57" (both parts).
S7: a week planned as a return-entry week stays one when its remaining days are rebuilt; every new exercise in it gets the entry dose in every time budget and follows the return steps.

D59 (met at R7A2-FREEZE-1 and at R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and at R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE and at STATE-EVIDENCE-FREEZE-1, closed): a return starts from the state at the break (stateAtBreak, strengthAtBreak): every exercise executed before the break’s first day is in use with its last performed date and, outside a return step and a phase reduction, its last executed whole count after the time fit (target met) as the ceiling (the largest of the break week, R20); a moderate or long return enters it at strengthEntrySets with strengthEntryMinimumRir or more, step 2 follows, the block in progress earns no set and the count comes back at most one set per executed whole week up to the ceiling; the progression the pre-break exposures earned stays unapplied. Regression: ssctr-r7a1-recheck-firstweek.mjs with E, O and B at 0 for NONE and FAMILIAR and O at 0 for KNOWN, my restoration, cap and short grids, and test "R7-A.2 I4/I5/I8 (SSCTR D59)". R7ASE-SSCTR-r1: the state at the break also takes the load the athlete lifted on a known-load row as the exercise’s load (lighter, or heavier only under D44: at most one smallest increment above the row and the row’s target met), a fact and never a step; an effort-guided row adopts nothing; a projected dose lifted exactly is that load with its repetition target and no further step. This approval excludes a stored load tick that counts an exposure the projection assumed and the athlete did not execute (NF-R7ASE-3, R42).
The readings of "the first quality slot still ahead" when other adaptations meet it, when the slot is not done and near a race are those of R7A1-SSCTR-QUALITY-SLOT-READINGS.

The start state of a return is the state at its interruption under R7A2-SSCTR-INTERRUPTION-STATE (revision R7ASE-SSCTR-r1), INTERRUPTION_EPISODE_CONTRACT R7AF-INTERRUPTION-1, WEEK_START_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT R7AB-WEEKSTART-1 (its record, temporal-contradiction rule and boundaries B1-B7, B9-B11) and STATE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT R7ASE-STATE-EVIDENCE-1: a correction names its interruption (episodeId) or repeats its days and starts from what the athlete had executed at its own start; a break after a re-entry or after training is new and starts from that re-entry plus the facts executed since; the state at the interruption is read value by value (one value per strength exercise, one for the run): a stored value counts only when its start holds that value as evidence decided before the cut (the intake, a return’s entry, the weekly review’s rule on that value’s historical value, or a projection whose own base value was historical and that the week before executed per sport exactly as assumed, loads included); a value a review carried from a projection is rebuilt by the review’s rule on its historical value; otherwise the value moves back to its last such start and the sessions executed after it are facts only (a known load lifted is the load under D44; a projected dose lifted is that load with its repetition target, never a load tick only the projection counted); weeks never reported are not history; a named correction that contradicts its own executed re-entry is asked; anything else is asked; each short break owns its easy slot.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

S-A (approved): an exercise first executed in the break’s week enters a moderate or long return at the entry, with its last executed whole count as the ceiling; E, O, B and ceiling disagreements at 0 in every class and length measured.

S-B (approved): after a short break a loaded exercise whose first log the break left unadopted is established by effort again (UNLOGGED, at most effortGuidedLoad.sets = 2, RIR 3 or more, at its executed repetitions); a bodyweight exercise set up before a short break continues at its normal count. Never above the last executed count or 2, never above the no-break timeline’s week.

S-C (approved as the declared reading): an exposure that missed its logged target is performed (in use) but gives no ceiling count; the ceiling falls back as declared (the earlier executed count, else the known count, else the normal count). Rises stay one set per executed whole week, gated on post-return targets (R36 records the met/missed asymmetry for the next policy revision).

S-D (approved): a re-establishment executed before a break is a fact: a moderate or long return takes the re-establishment count as the ceiling; after a short break the load is established by effort again (at most 2 sets, under the earlier load) and the count comes back one set per executed whole week (D53). R35 records the cost for the next policy revision.

S-E (approved): each short break owns its easy slot; a separate later short break takes the first quality slot still ahead that no break has eased (reading a: an eased run is no longer a quality slot), so when the first break’s slot is still ahead both run easy; a newer report of the same break keeps its slot; exactly one slot per break.

S-F (approved): a short break during the return steps resumes the step reached; a weekly review decided after the break began does not count, so the entry may repeat once (conservative); nothing returns to the dose before an earlier break. R7AB-SSCTR-r1: the step reached is the evidence-anchored one (WEEK_START_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT §3-§4); steps executed after the last evidence-anchored start are facts only, so on an unconsolidated re-entry week the entry may repeat after more than one executed week, and a strength-only shortfall also repeats the run entry (conservative; NF-R7AB-1, routed as R40). R7ASE-SSCTR-r1: the step reached is read value by value and per sport (STATE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT §4): a strength shortfall no longer repeats an executed run step, nor the reverse (R40 applied), and a value a review carried from a projection is rebuilt on history by the review’s rule.
S-G (approved): the entry repetition target of an exercise first executed before the break is the one it was executed at.

S-H (superseded by F-D): Training before the latest interruption logged after its return is confirmed first: while that return sets the plan (its re-entry week), every other report asks to confirm the interruption again, and the newer report reads the whole record (entry and ceiling as read in time). This replaces the R7-A.2 S-H/R37 boundary; the cost of what the pending question holds back is NF-R7AF-1 (routed, R38).

F-A (approved): a separate interruption after a re-entry starts from that re-entry plus the facts executed since, whatever reports of the earlier interruption came later; nothing returns to the dose before the earlier interruption; ceilings stay those of the first return.

F-B (approved): after an earlier interruption’s return, a re-entry week neither reviewed nor executed as planned is not a starting point; a later interruption starts from the re-entry plus the executed facts (the entry repeats, as S-F), on either side of a week boundary; a reviewed re-entry week’s decided start is used.

F-C (approved): A strength session on an interruption’s first day is ordered by the interruption’s stated start time: a session completed before that time is in the state (entry, that day’s count as the ceiling), one completed after it is not; with dates only it is asked when its order changes a fact the return starts from (in use, ceiling, unlogged load), and when only a last performed date differs the earlier date is kept (the conservative reading for a re-establishment threshold). This replaces the R7-A.2 NF-1 boundary.

F-D (approved, with NF-R7AF-1 routed as R38): Training before the latest interruption logged after its return is confirmed first: while that return sets the plan (its re-entry week), every other report asks to confirm the interruption again, and the newer report reads the whole record (entry and ceiling as read in time). This replaces the R7-A.2 S-H/R37 boundary; the cost of what the pending question holds back is NF-R7AF-1 (routed, R38).

F-E (approved): an interruption first reported after a later one began is that later interruption’s starting point (the start its report set; sessions between its end and its report belong to the plan before it, C5); a conservative reading.

F-F (approved as Founder-decided ASK, with NF-R7AF-2 routed as R39): a date-shifted correction without the interruption’s name is asked; a named one re-derives exactly as before; the same days are a duplicate; a clinical reason routes to qualified assessment before identity is considered.

D56, D57 and D58 hold on R7A2-FREEZE-1 and on R7A-FINAL-FREEZE and on R7A-BOUNDARY-FINAL-FREEZE and on STATE-EVIDENCE-FREEZE-1: no cap rises or ends after a week whose last exposure was not whole, no covered count comes back more than one set above the largest since the break, and the first quality slot still ahead of a short return runs easy, once per break.

R7AB S-A (approved): after an unfinished, unreviewed re-entry week, a later interruption starts from the re-entry plus the executed facts, whatever was decided meanwhile (equipment, fatigue, schedule, goal or event changes, a no-op statement); only the weekly review’s rule on the complete week, by a review or a handler applying it, may step what was executed in it, and the run holds when a run was missed.

R7AB S-B (approved, with NF-R7AB-1 routed as R40): completed sessions anchor a projected start only when the week executed exactly as the projection assumed, loads included; a lighter effort-guided load leaves the start to a review (which adopts it) or to the re-entry plus facts; a known load the athlete did not lift is never prescribed from a projection.

R7AB S-C (approved): a first interruption after an unconsolidated week moves back to the last evidence-anchored start; on a never-logged program this is the intake: runs from the intake capacity and return target, a known exercise at its reported load, an exercise never performed by the first-exposure establishment (D51, D52; effortGuidedLoad, at most 2 sets at RIR 3 or more), never a return step of a count or load the plan only assumed; with a known exercise in the return steps, exercises first set up in the entry week follow the entry (1 set, RIR 4 or more).
R7AB S-D (approved, with NF-R7AB-1): inside a return, a value a review held from a projected start is not history until a week is executed in full; a later short interruption resumes it at the entry.

R7AB S-E (approved as the Founder-decided ASK, §11): a named correction that puts its interruption on or after training executed after its own return began is asked when it changes a prescription; the plan in force stays the first return’s; no pre-break dose is restored.
R7AB S-F (approved): no unexecuted return step, load or whole count reaches a ceiling or a resumed dose through a stored start (D49, D53, D56).

R7ASE SE-A (approved): no prescription changes before a return: the R5 corpus, the profiles and the simulations are identical and the R6 holdout differs only in two returns after unreported weeks (H17, H26), with no status change; the planner is unchanged.

R7ASE SE-B (approved, with NF-R7ASE-1 routed as R41): a return starts from what the athlete executed, value by value, never from a value only a projection made (a load step, a load tick, a whole count or an easy week the plan assumed in a week not executed as assumed); after weeks never reported, the run value is the last evidence-anchored one and may sit below what reported weeks executed (conservative).

R7ASE SE-C (approved): in a week read as facts, a known load the athlete lifted on a known-load row is the exercise’s load: lighter, or heavier only under D44 (at most one smallest increment above the row, the row’s target met); a fact, never a step; an effort-guided row adopts nothing; history then equals what the weekly review would adopt.

R7ASE SE-D (approved with conditions, NF-R7ASE-3 routed as R42): a projected dose the athlete then lifted exactly is history for its load and for its repetitions as the target that goes with that load; with repetitions unlogged the load lifted is still the fact, the repetitions stay the target and no step is taken; a tick counted at a lower load is never carried onto the projected one. Not approved as history: a stored load tick at the lifted load that counts an exposure the projection assumed and the athlete did not execute; until R42, its sporting reach is bounded to the unchanged planner’s own no-break progression (one load step one successful exposure earlier, under the ceiling in a moderate or long return).

R7ASE SE-E (approved; R40 applied): per sport, a sport executed exactly as its projection assumed keeps its completed sessions when the other sport did not; never a step the sport did not execute; strength and run each equal or trail the reviewed control.

R7ASE SE-F (approved): a value a weekly review’s start carried from a projection is rebuilt by the review’s own rule on the historical value (never trusted whole, never walked back whole); a Sunday handler that applies the review’s rule is that sport’s review (E6), a Monday handler changes no history. SE-E and SE-F supersede the whole-start reading of R7AB S-B and S-D where they differ.
R7ASE SE-G (approved): a last performed date in history is the execution date; a re-establishment threshold read from history uses it.

R7ASE SE-H (approved as declared boundaries E1-E6, with NF-R7ASE-2 recorded): the planner reads the planning view (E1); a run value read through an unreviewed week keeps that week’s evidence start and is not re-gated (E2, unchanged); completed sessions verify a sport only when the whole week executed it as assumed (E3, my S-A); a rebuilt value reads the evidence known at the cut (E4); weeks never reported are not history and the planner keeps its plan (E5, cost NF-R7ASE-1); a last-day handler applying the review’s rule is that sport’s review (E6).
Weekly-review contract as in every record (R18).

Population, event-distance or V1 scope change.
Adverse event, runtime inconsistency or contrary comparable observations.
Founder funding declaration (move approved prescriptive records to HUMAN_REVALIDATION_REQUIRED).
